title: deontic dictionary
description: A lexicon's data half: everything a sentence can name, declared so that a sentence can be validated with nothing but the dictionary files. What a verb or metric means at evaluation time is the implementation's concern and is not here; a `description` on each is prose for people. Versioning is additive within a major: a consumer ignores what it does not know.

name.description: The dictionary's name; with `version` it is what a policy digest pins.

imports.description: Dictionaries whose declarations this one builds on. Names are resolved across all of them; a name declared twice is an error.

strictness.description: permissive: an unknown verb parses and the constraint is skipped; strict: anything unrecognised is an error.

types.description: Entity types, keyed by the singular name used in markers.

relations.description: Named relations recorded as {name, subject, object} triples rather than as a field of the subject. Keyed by relation name.

verbs.description: Verb declarations, keyed by the canonical verb phrase as it appears inside `@…@`.

events.description: Named date anchors for time expressions, keyed by the name used in markers.

cadences.description: Named periods a sentence may use in place of a literal (`every Inspection Period`).

metrics.description: Named measurements for the threshold shape, keyed by the name used in markers.

attesters.description: Attester kinds, keyed by the name used in markers.

definitions.description: Term and reference definitions shipped with the dictionary, as sentences in the storage form. They are parsed like any other definition; the names they define join the dictionary's names.

identifier.description: A name as it appears inside a marker: any text without sigils or quotes, whitespace-normalised.

field.description: Either a scalar kind as a bare string, or an object for a reference, a list, an optional field or one with a closed value set.

to.description: reference only: the target type. Traversed by the possessive.

optional.description: May be absent from a record. An absent field is `is empty`.

values.description: text only: the closed set of values, for editors and documentation. The corpus does not yet make an unlisted value an error.

plural.description: The form used inside `$$…$$`. Absent means the singular plus `s`.

tags.description: The closed set of tags a record of this type may carry and a sentence may name.

to.description: Object type. A relation is many-to-one: each subject has at most one object.

as.description: The word the possessive uses to traverse it from a subject (`dependency's file`). Absent means the object type's name.

synonyms.description: Other spellings accepted inside `@…@`; the parser records what was written, resolution maps it here.

subject.description: The type (or term) the subject must be. Absent means any.

object.description: `none`: the verb takes no object. `entity`: any type. Otherwise the type or term the object must be. Absent means `entity`.

description.description: What the verb means over recorded state, in prose. Not consumed by an implementation; it is what lets a second implementation reproduce the first's outcomes.

field.description: A date field of the type.

of.description: The type the metric is measured against.

unit.description: The unit of its value, when it has one (`percent`).

kind.description: `system` is a designated system, which judges under a rubric and records a confidence.

rubrics.description: system only: the rubrics this attester may judge under, keyed by rubric id. A sentence names one by id; an edit is a new version.

rubric.description: The written statement of what is assessed and by what criteria (design §9).

claim.description: What an attestation under this rubric asserts, in the language's own terms.

inputs.description: What the judge is given, and nothing else.

severities.description: The severity scale for findings, lowest first.

output.description: The output contract that becomes the attestation fact.

confidence.description: What a confidence value means under this rubric.

examples.description: Labelled examples that fix what a confidence value means.
